name: Djinn Cartography
description:
Formed in 2211 in the Shelf's flooded Calumet Ward, Djinn Cartography built their reputation playing illegal shows in decommissioned water treatment stations and under highway overpasses. The four-piece — fronted by vocalist and lyricist Seren Okafor-Vásquez, with Nkosi Threlfall on distorted kora-bass, Priya Holmqvist on percussion arrays, and Asel Brandt-Diallo on feedback guitar — play a ferocious hybrid of West African griot tradition, industrial noise, and broken-beat punk. Their sound is deliberately lo-fi, recorded on consumer hardware and distributed via pirate data chips pressed to look like transit tokens.

Their 2217 set at the Calumet Riot — a spontaneous uprising against a water reclamation corp — was broadcast live on pirate mesh and is considered one of the defining political performances in GLMZ history. Vantablack Media has issued seventeen formal takedown orders against their recordings, each one worn by the band as a badge of honor. Their song 'Shelf Liturgy' was spray-painted in phonetic notation across sixteen city blocks in Tier 1 by anonymous fans.
creator: Seren Okafor-Vásquez, Nkosi Threlfall, Priya Holmqvist, Asel Brandt-Diallo
audience: Shelf residents, anti-corporate activists, labor organizers in the Circuit, underground political cells
cultural_impact: Djinn Cartography are the closest thing the Shelf has to a house band for the revolution. Their music is not consumed so much as circulated — passed hand to hand on chips, hummed in work lines, played from cracked speakers in flooded corridors. Vantablack's repeated suppression attempts have made them mythological, and the band's refusal to negotiate with any label has become a political act in itself, inspiring a wave of self-distributed Shelf artists in the 2220s.
story_hooks: A player character receives a transit token that turns out to be a data chip containing an unreleased Djinn Cartography album — and someone is willing to kill to get it back.
Vantablack Media hires a fixer team to locate and 'silence' the band before a planned mass-broadcast concert; the team must decide whose side they're on.
Seren Okafor-Vásquez has gone missing days before the band's most ambitious show, and the remaining members suspect it was corporate extraction, not cold feet.
